The string table independently confirms 'bin/chr_b.bin' sits at exactly 0x0209F5D4, immediately preceded by koma.bin/komatxt.bin/kshape.bin and followed by chr_s.bin/ability.bin, matching the claimed load order verbatim.

Full disasm of 0x02077178 confirms recordBase = *(0x0214BD80)+0x40 + (PassiveIndex from [r1+0x41])*0x3C via the mla at 0x020771B8, then three ldrh reads at +8/+0xA/+0xC (statA/B/C) packed onto the stack (strh at 0x020771CC/D0/D4) and later compared with a bare 'cmp r3,sl' (0x02077288) -- addeq/lsleq/streq/lsreq on an equality match, not a threshold/tier compare, matching the claim's 'bare equality, not tier check' characterization and the prior-campaign movement.round1 cross-reference. Function is at 0x02077178 as claimed, immediately preceding 0x020772E4 in ROM.

The chr_b-caching half is real: 0x02077310-0x02077388 genuinely computes recordBase via mla, reads offset 0x10+4*idx as a byte (CombatStat low byte), clamps against 0x4000, and writes the result into BOTH r8+0x16 and r8+0x18 where r8 is a node walked from [charStruct+0x558] (confirmed by full disasm). But the claim that arm9 0x020784E4 (called from ov6 at 0x02158D8C) reads 'that SAME move-struct's +0x16/+0x18' is contradicted by independently-verified, exhaustively-traced cross-campaign evidence: damage-pipeline.round1 (GDB-proven) and guard-sp-gauges.round1 (exhaustive 8-site caller enumeration) establish that 0x020784E4's r4=[r0+0x56c] is a FIXED, single 'jpower' gauge pointer with its own dedicated, fully-enumerated call graph that never includes 0x020772E4/0x02077C0C; guard-sp-gauges further found the +0x558 list head is written ONLY by the one zero-init site ROM-wide (no store ever populates it with a live node), and its own walker (0x020783DC) is reached by only 2 call sites, disjoint from the 8 sites feeding +0x56c. +0x558 (dynamic list) and +0x56c (fixed pointer) are structurally and causally distinct objects; the claim's central 'cache-at-load feeds ov6 hit-resolution' linkage does not hold.

Full disasm of 0x02077768 confirms: r6=[sl+0x558] node, recordBase=*(0x0214BD80)+0x40+(node's own [r6+0x41])*0x3C, then a 5-iteration loop (sb=0..4, cmp sb,#5) reading record[3+sb] one byte at a time (0x020777CC: ldrb r1,[r1,#3] with r1=recordBase+sb) and using that raw byte value to index manager+0x50 (ldrb r0,[r2,r1,lsl#2]) to select among no-op(0)/direct-call-to-0x2077a74(1)/jump-table-via-r5(2+), exactly matching the claimed 3-way per-byte dispatch over offsets +3..+7 with no combined 32-bit load anywhere in this routine.

Full disasm of 0x02077C0C confirms every field mapping claimed: recordBase=*(0x0214BD80)+0x40+[r1+0x41]*0x3C; techIdx=[[r1+0x34]+8]-3; ldrb[r3+0x11] (high byte of CombatStat(techIdx+1)) -> cmp/moveq r3,#4 fallback -> strb[r1+0x49]; ldrb[r4+0x10] (low byte) -> lsl#6 -> strh[r1+0x16] -> reload+strh[r1+0x18] (duplicate); ldrsb[r2,#2]->strb[r1,#0x10] (KomaSize); ldrsb[r2,#1]->strb[r1,#0x11] (Tier); ldrb[r2]->strb[r1,#0x13] (FormType); ldrb[r4,#0x12]/[r4,#0x13]->strb[r1,#0x14]/[r1,#0x15] (CombatStatMod low/high); ldrh[r2,#0x30]->strh[r1,#0x2e] (TextIds[0]); ldrh[ip,#0x32]->strh[r1,#0x30] (TextIds[1+techIdx]). Every offset in the claim's dense field list is verified byte-for-byte against the disasm; the 'r1' move-struct target here is an independent function parameter (not the +0x558 list node from claim 2), so this claim does not depend on, and is not undermined by, the +0x558/+0x56c mismatch found in claim 2.

Disasm of 0x02078514 confirms recordBase=*(0x0214BD80)+0x40+PassiveIndex*0x3C, then 'add r0,r0,r1,lsl#1; ldrh r0,[r0,#0x24]' -- BattleParams read as ushort[6] (stride 2) starting at +0x24, exactly as claimed. Disasm at both call sites shows the return value immediately folded into a per-technique bitmask (tst against r8<<ip) and stored into a range/facing table (strh [r1+0xb4]) respectively, consistent with Battle-AI decision building. query.py strings ov11 --all (161 total strings) contains only BattleAI_*/'.cpp' debug labels and zero menu/UI-type strings, corroborating the 'Battle-AI subsystem, not menu' framing.

Full disasm of all three cited sites (0x0214D944, 0x0214DC18, 0x0214E480) confirms the identical pattern: a byte at koma+0xB is shifted right 4 and masked to isolate the high nibble, compared against 3, and on match computes recordBase=*(0x0214BD80)+0x40+(koma byte+7)*0x3C (via mla or smulbb) followed by a clean 'ldrb r0,[baseReg,idxReg]' reading record offset 0 (FormType), folded into a 16-bit sort/render key. The nibble!=3 branches in 0x0214D944/0x0214DC18 instead read chr_s at manager+0x48, matching the claim's contrast. All three FormType=offset-0 reads are directly, cleanly confirmed (not by analogy).

Disasm of both 0x0214E238 and 0x0214E284 confirms the base+stride setup (manager+0x40, mov/smulbb #0x3c) decodes cleanly as ARM, exactly as in claim 7's confirmed family. Immediately after the smulbb (0x0214E26C / 0x0214E2BC), the pre-built listing genuinely switches to 2-byte Thumb-style decode for several instructions before resyncing -- re-running query.py disasm fresh at the aligned address 0x0214E26C reproduces the identical anomalous decode, and the underlying bytes plainly contain the expected literal-pool word 0x0214BD80 misdecoded as Thumb 'pop {r7,pc}'/'80bd', confirming this is a disasm-listing artifact rather than genuine Thumb code (consistent with the SAME anomaly independently occurring at 0x0214E1E0 in claim 13's family). The claim correctly downgrades its own confidence to PLAUSIBLE rather than overclaiming CONFIRMED_STATIC, which is the right call given the evidence.

But the claim's core assertion -- that 0x020784E4 reads 'the SAME +0x16/+0x18 fields that arm9 0x020772E4 writes' -- inherits the same flaw identified in claim 2: 0x020784E4's target is a fixed jpower-gauge pointer at [x+0x56c] with an exhaustively-traced, disjoint call graph (per damage-pipeline/guard-sp-gauges), not the dynamically-walked +0x558 list-node object that 0x020772E4 populates. Part (1) NEGATIVE is confirmed correct (claim 9: ov6's sole direct hit touches manager+0x50, not chr_b). Part (3) POSITIVE-via-AI is confirmed correct (claims 5/6/11: ov11 reads BattleParams live through arm9 getters). But part (2) POSITIVE-via-caching -- 'ov6's actual hit-resolution function 0x02158B20 ... consumes a chr_b-derived value ... via this pre-computed cache' -- rests on the same +0x558-list-node vs +0x56c-fixed-pointer conflation refuted under claims 2 and 10: independently-traced evidence (damage-pipeline GDB-proven jpower gauge identity, guard-sp-gauges' exhaustive disjoint call-graph enumeration for +0x56c vs +0x558) contradicts the claim that these are the same object. The synthesis's headline 'NUANCED YES, via two distinct mechanisms' therefore overstates the case: only one mechanism (ov11 AI, architecturally not ov6) is actually confirmed positive; the ov6-specific caching link remains unproven and is more likely false than true.
